educationalModelNote: All numerical models are simplified educational models, not specifications of a real robot.

missions.title: TORQUE & INERTIA
missions.concept: Required joint torque depends on gravity, moment arm and rotational inertia; distal mass is disproportionately expensive.
missions.scenario: Hold and accelerate a loaded forearm while changing where the mass sits.
missions.goalText: Keep the same task under a 28 N·m joint envelope by manipulating mass distribution and acceleration.
missions.transferText: Recover torque margin after the tool shifts farther from the axis.

missions.title: MOTOR VS TRANSMISSION
missions.concept: A transmission trades motor speed for output torque and changes reflected inertia; motor capability cannot be read from output torque alone.
missions.scenario: Choose a reduction ratio for a joint that needs torque without becoming excessively slow or inertially heavy.
missions.goalText: Find a ratio that meets torque and speed while keeping reflected inertia controlled.
missions.transferText: Adapt the drivetrain to the higher speed requirement.

missions.title: GEAR RATIO TRADE-OFFS
missions.concept: Higher reduction multiplies torque but divides speed and squares reflected motor inertia; there is no universally best ratio.
missions.scenario: Tune a knee drivetrain for lift, agility and backdrivability at the same time.
missions.goalText: Find a balanced ratio instead of maximizing a single metric.
missions.transferText: Use the improved motor to recover more output torque without losing the inertia budget.

missions.title: CONTINUOUS VS PEAK
missions.concept: Peak torque is a short-duration capability; continuous capability is governed by thermal conditions and duty cycle.
missions.scenario: A crouch sequence passes one repetition but overheats during repeated use.
missions.goalText: Pass both the instantaneous torque limit and the thermal-duration limit.
missions.transferText: The peak rating did not change. Adapt torque demand or cooling to make repetition sustainable.

missions.title: POWER & THERMAL LIMITS
missions.concept: Torque, speed, electrical current and cooling form one operating envelope; repeated high-power motion can derate a healthy actuator.
missions.scenario: Run a fast lift without exceeding joint power or thermal reserve.
missions.goalText: Deliver useful torque while staying inside both power and thermal envelopes.

missions.title: ACTUATION GATE
missions.concept: Integrate torque, inertia, ratio, power and thermal reasoning instead of optimizing a joint by one headline number.
missions.scenario: Release a shoulder actuator package for three mission conditions.
missions.goalText: Complete the three actuator gate cases.

gateCases.name: STATIC + DYNAMIC LOAD
gateCases.text: Available output torque must exceed load torque by 20%.

gateCases.name: AGILITY
gateCases.text: Keep output speed proxy above 3 rad/s and reflected inertia below 0.14.

gateCases.name: POWER / THERMAL
gateCases.text: Keep mechanical power below 230 W while retaining at least 15 N·m torque margin.
